(212)

This nominal value 𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i}) will be crucial for the rest of our analysis. Using (16), we have that

|𝔼⁡[ℒN​(𝝁⋆1,…,𝝁⋆K,σ⋆2)]−𝔼⁡[ℒN​(𝒙1,…,𝒙N,0)]−d​σ⋆2​σt2αt2​σ⋆2+σt2|\displaystyle\left|\mathbb{E}\left[\mathcal{L}_{N}(\bm{\mu}_{\star}^{1},\dots,\bm{\mu}_{\star}^{K},\sigma_{\star}^{2})\right]-\mathbb{E}\left[\mathcal{L}_{N}(\bm{x}^{1},\dots,\bm{x}^{N},0)\right]-\frac{d\sigma_{\star}^{2}\sigma_{t}^{2}}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2}}\right| (213)
=1N​∑i=1N|𝔼⁡[‖𝒙¯⋆​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙¯mem​(t,𝒙ti)‖2]−d​σ⋆2​σt2αt2​σ⋆2+σt2|\displaystyle\quad=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left|\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\star}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{mem}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\right\rVert^{2}\right]-\frac{d\sigma_{\star}^{2}\sigma_{t}^{2}}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2}}\right| (214)
=1N​∑i=1N|𝔼⁡[‖𝒙¯⋆​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)+𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙i+𝒙i−𝒙¯mem​(t,𝒙ti)‖2]−d​σ⋆2​σt2αt2​σ⋆2+σt2|.\displaystyle\quad=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left|\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\star}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})+\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bm{x}_{i}+\bm{x}_{i}-\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{mem}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\right\rVert^{2}\right]-\frac{d\sigma_{\star}^{2}\sigma_{t}^{2}}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2}}\right|. (215)

In what follows, for simplicity, we denote Λti\Lambda_{t}^{i}

Λti=𝒙¯⋆​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)+𝒙i−𝒙¯mem​(t,𝒙ti).\Lambda_{t}^{i}=\bar{\bm{x}}_{\star}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})+\bm{x}_{i}-\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{mem}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i}). (216)

We have that

|𝔼⁡[ℒN​(𝝁⋆1,…,𝝁⋆K,σ⋆2)]−𝔼⁡[ℒN​(𝒙1,…,𝒙N,0)]−d​σ⋆2​σt2αt2​σ⋆2+σt2|\displaystyle\left|\mathbb{E}\left[\mathcal{L}_{N}(\bm{\mu}_{\star}^{1},\dots,\bm{\mu}_{\star}^{K},\sigma_{\star}^{2})\right]-\mathbb{E}\left[\mathcal{L}_{N}(\bm{x}^{1},\dots,\bm{x}^{N},0)\right]-\frac{d\sigma_{\star}^{2}\sigma_{t}^{2}}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2}}\right| (217)
=1N​∑i=1N|𝔼⁡[‖Λti+𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙i‖2]−d​σ⋆2​σt2αt2​σ⋆2+σt2|\displaystyle\quad=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left|\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\Lambda_{t}^{i}+\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bm{x}_{i}\right\rVert^{2}\right]-\frac{d\sigma_{\star}^{2}\sigma_{t}^{2}}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2}}\right| (218)
≤1N​∑i=1N|𝔼⁡[‖𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙i‖2]−d​σ⋆2​σt2αt2​σ⋆2+σt2|\displaystyle\quad\leq\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left|\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bm{x}_{i}\right\rVert^{2}\right]-\frac{d\sigma_{\star}^{2}\sigma_{t}^{2}}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2}}\right| (219)
+1N∑i=1N𝔼[‖Λti‖2]+2N∑i=1N𝔼[‖Λti‖2]1/2𝔼[‖𝒙¯nom(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙i‖2]1/2\displaystyle\qquad\quad+\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\Lambda_{t}^{i}\right\rVert^{2}\right]+\frac{2}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\Lambda_{t}^{i}\right\rVert^{2}\right]^{1/2}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bm{x}_{i}\right\rVert^{2}\right]^{1/2} (220)
≤1N​∑i=1N|𝔼⁡[‖𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙i‖2]−d​σ⋆2​σt2αt2​σ⋆2+σt2|\displaystyle\quad\leq\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left|\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bm{x}_{i}\right\rVert^{2}\right]-\frac{d\sigma_{\star}^{2}\sigma_{t}^{2}}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2}}\right| (221)
+2N∑i=1N{𝔼[‖𝒙¯⋆(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙¯nom(t,𝒙ti)‖2]+𝔼[‖𝒙i−𝒙¯mem(t,𝒙ti)‖2]}+\displaystyle\qquad\quad+\frac{2}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left\{\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\star}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\right\rVert^{2}\right]+\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bm{x}_{i}-\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{mem}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\right\rVert^{2}\right]\right\}+ (222)
4N​∑i=1N{𝔼⁡[‖𝒙¯⋆​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)‖2]+𝔼⁡[‖𝒙i−𝒙¯mem​(t,𝒙ti)‖2]}1/2\displaystyle\qquad\quad\frac{4}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left\{\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\star}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\right\rVert^{2}\right]+\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bm{x}_{i}-\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{mem}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\right\rVert^{2}\right]\right\}^{1/2} (223)
×𝔼​[‖𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙i‖2]1/2.\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad\times\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bm{x}_{i}\right\rVert^{2}\right]^{1/2}. (224)

In the rest of the proof, we control each term in (217).

Control of generalizing denoiser.

First, we are going to control 𝔼⁡[‖𝒙¯⋆​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)‖2]\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\star}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\right\rVert^{2}\right]. First, we recall that by (14)

𝒙¯⋆​(t,𝒙ti)=αt​σ⋆2αt2​σ⋆2+σt2​𝒙ti+σt2αt2​σ⋆2+σt2​∑i=1M𝝁i​softmax⁡(𝒘)i,\bar{\bm{x}}_{\star}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})=\frac{\alpha_{t}\sigma^{2}_{\star}}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma^{2}_{\star}+\sigma_{t}^{2}}\bm{x}_{t}^{i}+\frac{\sigma_{t}^{2}}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma^{2}_{\star}+\sigma_{t}^{2}}\sum_{i=1}^{M}\bm{\mu}^{i}\operatorname{softmax}(\bm{w})_{i}, (225)

In what follows, we denote

Γ=maxi∈[K]⁡‖μ⋆i‖.\Gamma=\max_{i\in[K]}\|\mu_{\star}^{i}\|. (226)

In addition, we have that

𝒙ti=αt​𝝁⋆ki+αt​σ⋆​𝒘+σt​𝒈​=𝑑​αt​𝝁⋆ki+(αt2​σ⋆2+σt2)1/2​𝒈.\bm{x}_{t}^{i}=\alpha_{t}\bm{\mu}_{\star}^{k_{i}}+\alpha_{t}\sigma_{\star}\bm{w}+\sigma_{t}\bm{g}\overset{d}{=}\alpha_{t}\bm{\mu}_{\star}^{k_{i}}+(\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2})^{1/2}\bm{g}. (227)

where kik_{i} is the index of the mean corresponding to 𝒙i\bm{x}^{i}. Finally, we have that for any p∈ℕp\in\mathbb{N}

𝔼⁡[‖𝒈‖p]≤𝔼​[‖𝒈‖2​p]1/2≤2p/2​(Γ⁡(d/2+p)/Γ⁡(d/2))1/2≤2p/2​(d/2+p)p/2.\mathbb{E}\left[\|\bm{g}\|^{p}\right]\leq\mathbb{E}\left[\|\bm{g}\|^{2p}\right]^{1/2}\leq 2^{p/2}(\Gamma(d/2+p)/\Gamma(d/2))^{1/2}\leq 2^{p/2}(d/2+p)^{p/2}. (228)

Combining those results, we get that for any p∈ℕp\in\mathbb{N}

𝔼⁡[‖𝒙ti‖p]≤22​p​(Γp+(αt2​σ⋆2+σt2)p/2​(d/2+p)p/2).\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bm{x}_{t}^{i}\right\rVert^{p}\right]\leq 2^{2p}\left(\Gamma^{p}+(\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2})^{p/2}(d/2+p)^{p/2}\right). (229)

Similarly, we have that for any p∈ℕp\in\mathbb{N}

𝔼⁡[‖𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)‖p]≤22​p​(Γp+(αt2​σ⋆2+σt2)p/2​(d/2+p)p/2).\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\right\rVert^{p}\right]\leq 2^{2p}\left(\Gamma^{p}+(\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2})^{p/2}(d/2+p)^{p/2}\right). (230)

For any event 𝖠\mathsf{A} such that ‖𝒙¯⋆​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)‖2≤C\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\star}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\right\rVert^{2}\leq C, we have that

𝔼⁡[‖𝒙¯⋆​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)‖2]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\star}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\right\rVert^{2}\right] ≤C​ℙ​[𝖠]+2​ℙ​[𝖠c]1/2​(𝔼​[‖𝒙ti‖4]1/2+𝔼​[‖𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)‖4]1/2)\displaystyle\leq C\mathbb{P}\left[\mathsf{A}\right]+2\mathbb{P}\left[\mathsf{A}^{\mathrm{c}}\right]^{1/2}\left(\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bm{x}_{t}^{i}\right\rVert^{4}\right]^{1/2}+\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\right\rVert^{4}\right]^{1/2}\right) (231)
≤C+16​(Γ2+(αt2​σ⋆2+σt2)​(d/2+4))​ℙ​[𝖠c]1/2.\displaystyle\leq C+16\left(\Gamma^{2}+(\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2})(d/2+4)\right)\mathbb{P}\left[\mathsf{A}^{\mathrm{c}}\right]^{1/2}. (232)

Now, combining this result and Section E.2 we get that

𝔼⁡[‖𝒙¯⋆​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)‖2]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\star}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\right\rVert^{2}\right] (233)
≤(2​K​σt2​maxk∈[K]​∥𝝁⋆k∥αt2​σ⋆2+σt2)2​exp⁡[−γ2​αt22​(αt2​σ⋆2+σt2)]\displaystyle\quad\leq\left(\frac{2K\sigma_{t}^{2}\max_{k\in[K]}\,\lVert\bm{\mu}_{\star}^{k}\rVert}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2}}\right)^{2}\exp\left[-\frac{\gamma^{2}\alpha_{t}^{2}}{2(\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2})}\right] (234)
+64(maxk∈[K]∥𝝁⋆k∥2+(αt2σ⋆2+σt2)(d/2+4))Kexp[−dε2/16].\displaystyle\qquad\quad+64\left(\max_{k\in[K]}\,\lVert\bm{\mu}_{\star}^{k}\rVert^{2}+(\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2})(d/2+4)\right)K\exp[-d\varepsilon^{2}/16]. (235)

Therefore, there exists a numerical constant C0≥0C_{0}\geq 0 such that

𝔼⁡[‖𝒙¯⋆​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)‖2]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\star}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\right\rVert^{2}\right] (236)
≤C0(maxk∈[K]∥𝝁⋆k∥2+(1+σ⋆2)d)K2(exp[−γ2​αt22​(αt2​σ⋆2+σt2)]+exp[−dε2/16]).\displaystyle\qquad\leq C_{0}\left(\max_{k\in[K]}\,\lVert\bm{\mu}_{\star}^{k}\rVert^{2}+(1+\sigma_{\star}^{2})d\right)K^{2}\left(\exp\left[-\frac{\gamma^{2}\alpha_{t}^{2}}{2(\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2})}\right]+\exp[-d\varepsilon^{2}/16]\right). (237)

Control of memorizing denoiser.

Second, we are going to control 𝔼⁡[‖𝒙i−𝒙¯mem​(t,𝒙ti)‖2]\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bm{x}_{i}-\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{mem}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\right\rVert^{2}\right]. The proof is similar to the control of 𝔼⁡[‖𝒙¯⋆​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)‖2]\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\star}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\right\rVert^{2}\right]. We recall that we have

𝒙¯mem​(t,𝒙t)=∑i=1N𝒙i​softmax⁡(𝒘)i,\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{mem}}(t,\bm{x}_{t})=\sum_{i=1}^{N}\bm{x}^{i}\operatorname{softmax}(\bm{w})_{i}, (238)

where

wi(𝒙t)=−12∥αt𝒙i−𝒙ti∥2/σt2w_{i}(\bm{x}_{t})=-\frac{1}{2}\|\alpha_{t}\bm{x}^{i}-\bm{x}_{t}^{i}\|^{2}/\sigma_{t}^{2} (239)

Similarly as before, we have for any p∈ℕp\in\mathbb{N}

𝔼⁡[maxi∈[N]⁡‖𝒙i‖p]≤22​p​N​(Γp+(d/2+p)p/2).\mathbb{E}\left[\max_{i\in[N]}\|\bm{x}_{i}\|^{p}\right]\leq 2^{2p}N(\Gamma^{p}+(d/2+p)^{p/2}). (240)

Therefore, we get that

𝔼⁡[‖𝒙i‖p]≤22​p​N​(Γp+σ⋆p​(d/2+p)p/2),𝔼⁡[‖𝒙¯mem​(t,𝒙ti)‖p]≤22​p​N​(Γp+σ⋆p​(d/2+p)p/2).\mathbb{E}\left[\|\bm{x}_{i}\|^{p}\right]\leq 2^{2p}N(\Gamma^{p}+\sigma_{\star}^{p}(d/2+p)^{p/2}),\qquad\mathbb{E}\left[\|\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{mem}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\|^{p}\right]\leq 2^{2p}N(\Gamma^{p}+\sigma_{\star}^{p}(d/2+p)^{p/2}). (241)

Note that this upper-bound is rather loose but given the rate of growth of NN with respect to dd that we will consider we won’t need a tighter bound. For any event 𝖠\mathsf{A} such that ‖𝒙¯mem​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙i‖2≤C\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{mem}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bm{x}^{i}\right\rVert^{2}\leq C, we have that

𝔼⁡[‖𝒙¯mem​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙i‖2]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{mem}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bm{x}^{i}\right\rVert^{2}\right] ≤C​ℙ​[𝖠]+2​ℙ​[𝖠c]1/2​(𝔼​[‖𝒙ti‖4]1/2+𝔼​[‖𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)‖4]1/2)\displaystyle\leq C\mathbb{P}\left[\mathsf{A}\right]+2\mathbb{P}\left[\mathsf{A}^{\mathrm{c}}\right]^{1/2}\left(\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bm{x}_{t}^{i}\right\rVert^{4}\right]^{1/2}+\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\right\rVert^{4}\right]^{1/2}\right) (242)
≤C+16​(Γ2+σ⋆2​(d/2+4))​ℙ​[𝖠c]1/2.\displaystyle\leq C+16\left(\Gamma^{2}+\sigma_{\star}^{2}(d/2+4)\right)\mathbb{P}\left[\mathsf{A}^{\mathrm{c}}\right]^{1/2}. (243)

Therefore, combining this result with Section E.2, there exists a numerical constant C1≥0C_{1}\geq 0 such that

𝔼⁡[‖𝒙¯mem​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙i‖2]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{mem}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bm{x}^{i}\right\rVert^{2}\right] (244)
≤C1(maxk∈[K]∥𝝁⋆k∥2+(1+σ⋆2)d)N2(exp[−αt2​σ⋆2​(1−ε)​d2​σt2]+exp[−dε2/16]).\displaystyle\qquad\leq C_{1}\left(\max_{k\in[K]}\,\lVert\bm{\mu}_{\star}^{k}\rVert^{2}+(1+\sigma_{\star}^{2})d\right)N^{2}\left(\exp\left[-\frac{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}(1-\varepsilon)d}{2\sigma_{t}^{2}}\right]+\exp[-d\varepsilon^{2}/16]\right). (245)

Control of the nominal expectation.

For the nominal error ∥𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙i∥\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bm{x}^{i}\rVert, we have by the nominal denoiser’s definition in Section E.2 and the distributional assumption 𝒙i∼i.i.d.π\bm{x}^{i}\sim_{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}\pi

‖𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙i‖2\displaystyle\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bm{x}^{i}\right\rVert^{2} =‖αt​σ⋆2αt2​σ⋆2+σt2​𝒙ti+σt2αt2​σ⋆2+σt2​𝝁⋆ki−𝒙i‖2\displaystyle=\left\lVert\frac{\alpha_{t}\sigma_{\star}^{2}}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2}}\bm{x}_{t}^{i}+\frac{\sigma_{t}^{2}}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2}}\bm{\mu}_{\star}^{k_{i}}-\bm{x}^{i}\right\rVert^{2} (246)
=‖αt2​σ⋆2αt2​σ⋆2+σt2​σ⋆​𝒘i+αt​σ⋆2αt2​σ⋆2+σt2​σt​𝒈i−σ⋆​𝒘i‖2,\displaystyle=\left\lVert\frac{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2}}\sigma_{\star}\bm{w}^{i}+\frac{\alpha_{t}\sigma_{\star}^{2}}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2}}\sigma_{t}\bm{g}^{i}-\sigma_{\star}\bm{w}^{i}\right\rVert^{2}, (247)

where 𝒘i∼𝒩⁡(𝟎,𝑰)\bm{w}^{i}\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\bm{I}) is independent of 𝒈i∼𝒩⁡(𝟎,𝑰)\bm{g}^{i}\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\bm{I}). In particular, this is equal in distribution to the squared ℓ2\ell^{2} norm of a Gaussian random variable, which has zero mean and isotropic diagonal covariance with diagonal elements

σ⋆2​(1−αt2​σ⋆2αt2​σ⋆2+σt2)2+σt2​(αt​σ⋆2αt2​σ⋆2+σt2)2=σ⋆2​σt2αt2​σ⋆2+σt2.\displaystyle\sigma_{\star}^{2}\left(1-\frac{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2}}\right)^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2}\left(\frac{\alpha_{t}\sigma_{\star}^{2}}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2}}\right)^{2}=\frac{\sigma_{\star}^{2}\sigma_{t}^{2}}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2}}. (248)

An application of Section C.1 then gives that with probability at least 1−2exp[−dε2/8]1-2\exp[-d\varepsilon^{2}/8]

|‖𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙i‖2−d​σ⋆2​σt2αt2​σ⋆2+σt2|≤ε​d​σ⋆2​σt2αt2​σ⋆2+σt2\left\lvert\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bm{x}^{i}\right\rVert^{2}-\frac{d\sigma_{\star}^{2}\sigma_{t}^{2}}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2}}\right\rvert\leq\varepsilon\frac{d\sigma_{\star}^{2}\sigma_{t}^{2}}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2}} (249)

For any event 𝖠\mathsf{A} such that

|‖𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙i‖2−d​σ⋆2​σt2αt2​σ⋆2+σt2|≤C,\left\lvert\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bm{x}^{i}\right\rVert^{2}-\frac{d\sigma_{\star}^{2}\sigma_{t}^{2}}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2}}\right\rvert\leq C, (250)

on that event, we have that

|𝔼⁡[‖𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙i‖2]−d​σ⋆2​σt2αt2​σ⋆2+σt2|≤𝔼⁡[|‖𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙i‖2−d​σ⋆2​σt2αt2​σ⋆2+σt2|]\displaystyle\left\lvert\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bm{x}^{i}\right\rVert^{2}\right]-\frac{d\sigma_{\star}^{2}\sigma_{t}^{2}}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2}}\right\rvert\leq\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lvert\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bm{x}^{i}\right\rVert^{2}-\frac{d\sigma_{\star}^{2}\sigma_{t}^{2}}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2}}\right\rvert\right] (251)
≤C+ℙ​[𝖠c]1/2​(𝔼​[‖𝒙i‖4]1/2+𝔼​[‖𝒙¯nom​(t,𝒙ti)‖4]1/2)\displaystyle\qquad\leq C+\mathbb{P}\left[\mathsf{A}^{\mathrm{c}}\right]^{1/2}\left(\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bm{x}^{i}\right\rVert^{4}\right]^{1/2}+\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\right\rVert^{4}\right]^{1/2}\right) (252)

Therefore, there exists C2≥0C_{2}\geq 0, a numerical constant, such that

Proof.

First note that ε=Θ⁡(log⁡(d)/d1/2)\varepsilon=\Theta(\log(d)/d^{1/2}) satisfies the coupling condition. Next, if we assume that dd is large enough so that 1−ε≤1/21-\varepsilon\leq 1/2. We have

|𝔼⁡[ℒN​(𝝁⋆1,…,𝝁⋆K,σ⋆2)]−𝔼⁡[ℒN​(𝒙1,…,𝒙N,0)]−d​σ⋆2​σt2αt2​σ⋆2+σt2|\displaystyle\left|\mathbb{E}\left[\mathcal{L}_{N}(\bm{\mu}_{\star}^{1},\dots,\bm{\mu}_{\star}^{K},\sigma_{\star}^{2})\right]-\mathbb{E}\left[\mathcal{L}_{N}(\bm{x}^{1},\dots,\bm{x}^{N},0)\right]-\frac{d\sigma_{\star}^{2}\sigma_{t}^{2}}{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}+\sigma_{t}^{2}}\right| (263)

×exp⁡[−116​min⁡(log⁡(d)2,ψt​σ⋆2​d,γ2​ψt1+σ⋆2​ψt)].\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\times\exp\left[-\frac{1}{16}\min\left(\log(d)^{2},\psi_{t}\sigma_{\star}^{2}d,\frac{\gamma^{2}\psi_{t}}{1+\sigma_{\star}^{2}\psi_{t}}\right)\right]. (265)

Proof.

The proof will be an application of Section E.2 and Section E.2.

Softmax value decomposition.

Using (16), we have that

𝔼⁡[ℒN​(𝒙1,…,𝒙ℓ,0)]−𝔼⁡[ℒN​(𝒙1,…,𝒙N,0)]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\mathcal{L}_{N}(\bm{x}^{1},\dots,\bm{x}^{\ell},0)\right]-\mathbb{E}\left[\mathcal{L}_{N}(\bm{x}^{1},\dots,\bm{x}^{N},0)\right] (272)
=1N​∑i=1N𝔼⁡[‖𝒙¯pmem,M​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙¯mem​(t,𝒙ti)‖2]\displaystyle\quad=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{pmem},M}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{mem}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\right\rVert^{2}\right] (273)
=1N​∑i=1N𝔼⁡[‖𝒙¯pmem,M​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙i+𝒙i−𝒙¯mem​(t,𝒙ti)‖2].\displaystyle\quad=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{pmem},M}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bm{x}_{i}+\bm{x}_{i}-\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{mem}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\right\rVert^{2}\right]. (274)

We have that

=1N​∑i=1N𝔼⁡[‖𝒙¯pmem,M​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙i+𝒙i−𝒙¯mem​(t,𝒙ti)‖2]\displaystyle\qquad=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{pmem},M}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bm{x}_{i}+\bm{x}_{i}-\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{mem}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\right\rVert^{2}\right] (276)
=1N​∑i=1N𝔼⁡[‖𝒙¯pmem,M​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙i‖2]+𝔼⁡[‖𝒙¯mem​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙i‖2]+2​Λti,\displaystyle\qquad=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{pmem},M}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bm{x}^{i}\right\rVert^{2}\right]+\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{mem}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bm{x}^{i}\right\rVert^{2}\right]+2\Lambda_{t}^{i}, (277)

where

|Λti|≤𝔼​[‖𝒙¯mem​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙i‖2]1/2​𝔼​[‖𝒙¯pmem,M​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙i‖2]1/2.|\Lambda_{t}^{i}|\leq\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{mem}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bm{x}^{i}\right\rVert^{2}\right]^{1/2}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{pmem},M}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bm{x}^{i}\right\rVert^{2}\right]^{1/2}. (278)

In the rest of the proof, we control each term in (217).

Second, we are going to control 𝔼⁡[‖𝒙i−𝒙¯mem​(t,𝒙ti)‖2]\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bm{x}_{i}-\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{mem}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\right\rVert^{2}\right]. The proof is similar to the one of Appendix F but we reproduce it for completeness. We recall that we have

𝒙¯mem​(t,𝒙t)=∑i=1N𝒙i​softmax⁡(𝒘)i,\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{mem}}(t,\bm{x}_{t})=\sum_{i=1}^{N}\bm{x}^{i}\operatorname{softmax}(\bm{w})_{i}, (279)

where

wi(𝒙t)=−12∥αt𝒙i−𝒙ti∥2/σt2w_{i}(\bm{x}_{t})=-\frac{1}{2}\|\alpha_{t}\bm{x}^{i}-\bm{x}_{t}^{i}\|^{2}/\sigma_{t}^{2} (280)

Similarly as before, we have for any p∈ℕp\in\mathbb{N}

Note that this upper-bound is rather loose but given the rate of growth of NN with respect to dd that we will consider we won’t need a tighter bound. For any event 𝖠\mathsf{A} such that ‖𝒙¯mem​(t,𝒙ti)−𝒙i‖2≤C\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{mem}}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\bm{x}^{i}\right\rVert^{2}\leq C, we have that

Therefore, combining this result with Section E.2, there exists a numerical constant C1≥0C_{1}\geq 0 such that

≤C1(maxk∈[K]∥𝝁⋆k∥2+(1+σ⋆2)d)N2(exp[−αt2​σ⋆2​(1−ε)​d2​σt2]+exp[−dε2/16]).\displaystyle\qquad\leq C_{1}\left(\max_{k\in[K]}\,\lVert\bm{\mu}_{\star}^{k}\rVert^{2}+(1+\sigma_{\star}^{2})d\right)N^{2}\left(\exp\left[-\frac{\alpha_{t}^{2}\sigma_{\star}^{2}(1-\varepsilon)d}{2\sigma_{t}^{2}}\right]+\exp[-d\varepsilon^{2}/16]\right). Third, we are going to control 𝔼⁡[‖𝒙i−𝒙¯pmem,M​(t,𝒙ti)‖2]\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\bm{x}_{i}-\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{pmem},M}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})\right\rVert^{2}\right]. First, similarly as before, we have that

=‖𝒙¯pmem,M​(t,𝒙ti)−∑j∈𝖲isoftmax⁡(𝒘|𝖲i)j​𝒙j‖2\displaystyle=\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{pmem},M}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\sum_{j\in\mathsf{S}_{i}}\operatorname{softmax}(\bm{w}|_{\mathsf{S}_{i}})_{j}\bm{x}^{j}\right\rVert^{2} (294)
+‖∑j∈𝖲isoftmax⁡(𝒘|𝖲i)j​𝒙j−𝒙i‖2\displaystyle\qquad+\left\lVert\sum_{j\in\mathsf{S}_{i}}\operatorname{softmax}(\bm{w}|_{\mathsf{S}_{i}})_{j}\bm{x}^{j}-\bm{x}^{i}\right\rVert^{2} (295)
+2​⟨𝒙¯pmem,M​(t,𝒙ti)−∑j∈𝖲isoftmax⁡(𝒘|𝖲i)j​𝒙j,∑j∈𝖲isoftmax⁡(𝒘|𝖲i)j​𝒙j−𝒙i⟩\displaystyle\qquad\quad+2\left\langle\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{pmem},M}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\sum_{j\in\mathsf{S}_{i}}\operatorname{softmax}(\bm{w}|_{\mathsf{S}_{i}})_{j}\bm{x}^{j},\sum_{j\in\mathsf{S}_{i}}\operatorname{softmax}(\bm{w}|_{\mathsf{S}_{i}})_{j}\bm{x}^{j}-\bm{x}^{i}\right\rangle (296)

+‖𝒙¯pmem,M​(t,𝒙ti)−∑j∈𝖲isoftmax⁡(𝒘|𝖲i)j​𝒙j‖​‖∑j∈𝖲isoftmax⁡(𝒘|𝖲i)j​𝒙j−𝒙i‖\displaystyle\qquad+\left\lVert\bar{\bm{x}}_{\mathrm{pmem},M}(t,\bm{x}_{t}^{i})-\sum_{j\in\mathsf{S}_{i}}\operatorname{softmax}(\bm{w}|_{\mathsf{S}_{i}})_{j}\bm{x}^{j}\right\rVert\left\lVert\sum_{j\in\mathsf{S}_{i}}\operatorname{softmax}(\bm{w}|_{\mathsf{S}_{i}})_{j}\bm{x}^{j}-\bm{x}^{i}\right\rVert (299)

Appendix G Additional Related Work

Memorization in diffusion models.

Understanding memorization and generalization properties of diffusion models is crucial for practitioners [Somepalli et al., 2023, Ren et al., 2024, Rahman et al., 2024, Wang et al., 2024a, Chen et al., 2024b, Stein et al., 2024]. Indeed, concerns about privacy [Ghalebikesabi et al., 2023, Carlini et al., 2023, Nasr et al., 2023] and copyright infringement [Cui et al., 2023, Wang et al., 2024a, Vyas et al., 2023, Franceschelli and Musolesi, 2022] are key issues as these models are deployed. Several factors can influence the memorization capabilities of diffusion models. Duplication and out-of-distribution samples have been shown to lead to replication in diffusion models [Carlini et al., 2023, Ross et al., 2024, Webster, 2023] and solutions have been proposed by curating the dataset [Chen et al., 2024a] or introducing dummy data and adapting diffusion models to unseen data [Daras et al., 2024, Yoon et al., 2023]. Neural network architectures have also been shown to play a role in memorization with [Chavhan et al., 2024] identifying specific neurons causing memorization and [Wen et al., 2024, Wang et al., 2024b] analyzing variability in the prediction function to identify problematic prompts in image models. We refer to [Gu et al., 2023] for an in-depth experimental investigation of those issues. Finally, we highlight the work of [Kadkhodaie et al., 2023], in which the authors investigate the inductive bias image denoisers to investigate the generalization properties of state-of-the-art diffusion models.

Definitions of memorization.

Note that our definition of memorization (Section 2) is connected to the one of Eidetic Memorization as introduced by Carlini et al. [2023]. Similarly, to [Carlini et al., 2023], we acknowledge that this notion of memorization is strong as it implies that an image is memorized if there exists a near perfect copy in the training dataset which does not fully capture copyright infringement or data privacy issues. We refer to [Elkin-Koren et al., 2023] for an in-depth discussion of those issues.

Memorization and overfitting.

A priori, it may not be clear why memorization in diffusion models is substantially different from overfitting which has been a long-standing and well-studied property of machine learning systems Hastie et al. [2009]. Overfitting is characterized by a large gap between training and validation losses. However, overfitting is not directly connected to memorization. For a small number of parameters, the partially memorizing denoisers defined in Section 3 have large training and validation losses which ultimately have a small gap, meaning that such models are not significantly overfit; however, every single sample they generate is memorized. Meanwhile, the model corresponding to the fully memorizing denoiser defined in Section 2 is both very overfit and does memorize. It is also worthwhile to discuss the connection of diffusion model memorization with benign overfitting [Bartlett et al., 2020] and double descent [Belkin et al., 2019]. In particular, we wish to clarify why the setting of diffusion models may be separated from benign overfitting. The core difference is as follows: in the usual double descent setting, one studies an overparameterized learning problem, such as regression or classification, and there are many models at a fixed parameter count which obtain the minimal training loss; then it is up to (implicit) regularization to choose the best solution, which benignly interpolates the training data. As the number of parameters increase, the training loss of the trained model never increases, and the validation loss eventually also decreases (after an initial increase for the purpose of overfitting). Meanwhile, in the case of diffusion, there is exactly one model which obtains the minimal training loss, which is the memorizing denoiser, and this does not change no matter how many parameters are allocated. Certainly the memorizing denoiser does not benignly interpolate the training data. As the number of parameters increase past a certain point, the training loss never decreases, and in fact may increase, showing that double descent or benign overfitting indeed do not apply straightforwardly to the case of diffusion.

Appendix H Experimental Details

We run all experiments on several Nvidia A100 80GB GPUs using Jax 0.6.0 and Equinox 0.12 [Kidger and Garcia, 2021]. Each training/evaluation job occurs on a single A100 and the results are saved to file to be aggregated later. Aggregation, analysis, and visualization occur on a single A100.

H.1 Datasets, Optimization, and Initialization Details

In our experiments in Section 4.1, we generate synthetic Gaussian mixture models, by generating the KK means 𝝁⋆i\bm{\mu}_{\star}^{i} uniformly on the sphere of radius d\sqrt{d} and setting the ground truth variance σ⋆2=1\sigma_{\star}^{2}=1, as prescribed by the results in Section 3. The experiments conducted in Figures 1, 2 and 6 are all under the setting N=200N=200, d=50d=50, and K=12K=12. For the sweep in Figure 3 we take (N,d,K)(N,d,K) tuples from [50,100,150,200]×[30,40,50,60]×[3,6,9,12][50,100,150,200]\times[30,40,50,60]\times[3,6,9,12], obtaining a total of 64 (N,d,K)(N,d,K) tuples. For each setting of (N,d,K)(N,d,K) (including the sweep in Figure 3) we train 20 models at different model sizes MM: starting from M=⌊N/10⌋M=\lfloor N/10\rfloor and moving in increments of ⌊N/10⌋\lfloor N/10\rfloor to M=10​⌊N/10⌋M=10\lfloor N/10\rfloor; then, training 10 more models where MM is equally spaced between the MM where the phase transition starts and the MM where it ends (using the empirical criterion in Section 4).

In our experiments in Section 4.2, we generate synthetic colored FashionMNIST data by sampling KK FashionMNIST [Xiao et al., 2017] images uniformly at random to use as “templates”, then using the PIL (Pillow) utility to reshape them to 15×1515\times 15 resolution. For each of the KK templates (components) we generate a color vector using a Gaussian with ground truth mean and variance (𝒖⋆i,𝝈⋆2)=(𝟎,1)∈ℝ3×ℝ(\bm{u}_{\star}^{i},\bm{\sigma}_{\star}^{2})=(\bm{0},1)\in\mathbb{R}^{3}\times\mathbb{R}. We take the Kronecker product of the color vector and the template as described in Section 4.2 in order to form the sample. Figure 4 uses the setting N=K=8N=K=8 while the experiment in Figure 5 uses the setting N=100N=100, K=4K=4, and color dimension d=3d=3. Here we train 1010 models at different model sizes MM, starting from M=⌊N/10⌋M=\lfloor N/10\rfloor and moving in increments of ⌊N/10⌋\lfloor N/10\rfloor to M=10​⌊N/10⌋M=10\lfloor N/10\rfloor.

For all experiments, we use the “variance preserving” process which yields αt=1−t2\alpha_{t}=\sqrt{1-t^{2}} and σt=t\sigma_{t}=t for t∈[0,1]t\in[0,1]. We use the objective (6) to train our model denoisers. For training, we always train with the loss weighting λ⁡(t):=αt2/σt2\lambda(t):=\alpha_{t}^{2}/\sigma_{t}^{2}, which is equivalent to using noise prediction ([Karras et al., 2022]), and t∼Unif⁡((tℓ)ℓ=0L)t\sim\operatorname{Unif}((t_{\ell})_{\ell=0}^{L}) where we use L=25L=25 decreasing timesteps tℓ=0.01+0.998​(L−ℓ)/L=0.999−0.998​ℓ/L∈(0,1)t_{\ell}=0.01+0.998(L-\ell)/L=0.999-0.998\ell/L\in(0,1). In lieu of computing the (obviously intractable) inner expectation in ℒN,t\mathcal{L}_{N,t}, we use Ndup:=100N_{\mathrm{dup}}:=100 Gaussian noise draws for each of the NN samples to estimate the expectation. We use full-batch Adam for NepochsN_{\mathrm{epochs}} epochs (also, iterations) to optimize the objective; for experiments in Section 4.1 we have Nepochs=50,000N_{\mathrm{epochs}}=50,000 and for experiments in Section 4.2 we have Nepochs=100,000N_{\mathrm{epochs}}=100,000. We use a “warmup-decay” learning rate schedule: for Nwarmup:=Nepochs/10N_{\mathrm{warmup}}:=N_{\mathrm{epochs}}/10 epochs the learning rate linearly increases from 00 to 10−310^{-3}; for the remaining Ndecay:=Nepochs−NwarmupN_{\mathrm{decay}}:=N_{\mathrm{epochs}}-N_{\mathrm{warmup}} epochs the learning rate linearly decreases from 10−310^{-3} to 10−610^{-6}.

For all models we train, we use a “partial memorization initialization” along with the Adam optimizer We use this initialization because the loss at a truly random initialization is extremely high, in many cases often at least eight orders of magnitude larger than the loss at optimum, and Adam is often unable to learn effectively given this massive conditioning. The partial memorizing initialization, in the context of the isotropic Gaussian mixture model, sets the initial σ2\sigma^{2} to 10−610^{-6}, and each mean 𝝁i\bm{\mu}^{i} to a random sample. In the context of the simple image model, it sets each initial template parameter 𝑨𝒙i\bm{A}_{\bm{x}^{i}} to the template which generates a sample, the corresponding initial color vector to the unique vector which generates the (not identically zero) sample given that template, and the initial color variance σ2\sigma^{2} to 10−610^{-6}. Notice that in the experiments such as Figure 2, even models initialized with this partial memorizing initialization end up learning (nearly) generalizing solutions — unless of course it is more favorable to memorize, which occurs with very large MM.

We use the implementation of the DDIM sample prescribed in De Bortoli et al. [2025], i.e., using the above notation and given a denoiser 𝒙¯\bar{\bm{x}}

H.3 Formal Description of Loss Weighting Regression

Recall that in Section 4.1 we predicted the phase transition using the loss approximations derived in Section 3. To do this, we solved a regression problem (22). Here, we will discuss how we solve this problem efficiently by smoothing and regularization.

Namely, as a bilevel semi-discrete quadratic program, the problem (22) is hard to optimize outright via gradient methods. As a result we parameterize the distribution over MM via a temperature-weighted softmax with high temperature τ=1/20\tau=1/20, placing an entropy penalty (βsparsity=10−3\beta_{\mathrm{sparsity}}=10^{-3}) on the softmax output to ensure that the learned distribution over MM is sparse. The overall problem is (using the notation from (22))

minλ~\displaystyle\min_{\tilde{\lambda}}\quad ∑(N,d,K)(M¯pt​(N,d,K,λ~)N−MptN)2\displaystyle\sum_{(N,d,K)}\left(\frac{\bar{M}_{\mathrm{pt}}(N,d,K,\tilde{\lambda})}{N}-\frac{M_{\mathrm{pt}}}{N}\right)^{2} (311)
−βsparsity∑(N,d,K)∑Mp~(N,d,K,M,λ~)logp~(N,d,K,M,λ~)\displaystyle\qquad-\beta_{\mathrm{sparsity}}\sum_{(N,d,K)}\sum_{M}\tilde{p}(N,d,K,M,\tilde{\lambda})\log\tilde{p}(N,d,K,M,\tilde{\lambda}) (312)
where M¯pt​(N,d,K,λ~)=∑MM⋅p~​(N,d,K,M,λ~)\displaystyle\bar{M}_{\mathrm{pt}}(N,d,K,\tilde{\lambda})=\sum_{M}M\cdot\tilde{p}(N,d,K,M,\tilde{\lambda}) (313)
and p~(N,d,K,⋅,λ~)=softmax({−1τ(∑ℓ=0Lλ~(tℓ)(LˇN,t(θpmem,M(N,d,K))−LˇN,t(θ⋆(N,d,K)))2}M)\displaystyle\tilde{p}(N,d,K,\cdot,\tilde{\lambda})=\resizebox{14131200}{}{$\operatorname{softmax}\mathopen{}\left(\left\{-\frac{1}{\tau}\left(\sum_{\ell=0}^{L}\tilde{\lambda}(t_{\ell})(\check{L}_{N,t}(\theta_{\mathrm{pmem},M}(N,d,K))-\check{L}_{N,t}(\theta_{\star}(N,d,K))\right)^{2}\right\}_{M}\right)$} (314)

In all cases, when we report the loss we refer to just the MSE component described in (311).

H.5 More Experimental Results

Interpreting the learned models.

In this section we take advantage of the white-box nature of our denoiser and specifically how it relates to the data generating process, to try to uncover some mechanistic aspects of memorization in this setup. There are two questions we wish to answer:

  • •

    Is the learned variance σtrain2\sigma_{\mathrm{train}}^{2} an effective proxy for memorization or generalization?

  • •

    How do the learned means 𝝁traini\bm{\mu}_{\mathrm{train}}^{i} behave in memorized and generalized models?

Recall that the ground truth (generalizing) denoiser has variance σ⋆2\sigma_{\star}^{2} and means 𝝁⋆i\bm{\mu}_{\star}^{i}, and the memorizing denoiser has variance 00 and means 𝒙i\bm{x}^{i}. Thus, one intuition would be that a smaller variance implies a propensity of the trained model to memorize, and learned means closer to samples would imply the same. To verify this behavior we plot the learned variance and the average distance of the learned means to training samples and ground truth means, respectively, in Figure 6. We can confirm that our basic intuition is true, with a twist: while the learned variance σtrain2\sigma_{\mathrm{train}}^{2} decreases as the model size MM increases, it does so linearly, and even in the generalization regime. Similarly the average distance of each learned mean to the closest point in the training dataset decreases linearly to 00. In this sense, these and other mechanistically derived quantities may serve as a continuous proxy for the rapid phase transition, a behavior also observed in large models with far more complicated “circuits” [Nanda et al., 2023, Schaeffer et al., 2023].

Assessing the variance of different seeds.

In Figure 7, we examine multiple runs using different random seeds to see their effect on the loss and memorization plots (akin to Figure 1). The shading on the memorization plot, which showcases the minimum and maximum value of the quantity across three seeds, amounts to error bars on the regression experiment in Figure 3, since the approximated losses will be the same (as they are computed deterministically), and the only remaining variation is the regression target, i.e., the location of the phase transition.
